revelation.excerpt: Friend, he that stands before thee was that child. HERDSMAN. A plague upon thee! Hold thy wanton tongue! OEDIPUS. Softly, old man, rebuke him not; thy words Are more deserving chastisement than his. HERDSMAN. O best of masters, what is my offense? OEDIPUS. Not answering what he asks about the child. HERDSMAN. He speaks at random, babbles like a fool. OEDIPUS. If thou lack’st grace to speak, I’ll loose thy tongue. HERDSMAN. For mercy’s sake abuse not an old man. OEDIPUS. Arrest the villain, seize and pinion him! HERDSMAN. Alack, alack! What have I done? what wouldst thou further learn? OEDIPUS. Didst give this man the child of whom he asks? HERDSMAN. I did; and would that I had died that day!

narrativeBlocks.title: The plague and the promise
narrativeBlocks.body: Thebes is dying — crops fail, women miscarry, the city begs its king. Oedipus, who saved Thebes once by answering the Sphinx's riddle, sends to Delphi: the oracle says the plague lives because the city shelters the murderer of old King Laius, unpunished.

narrativeBlocks.title: The detective-king
narrativeBlocks.body: Oedipus does not hesitate: he curses the killer, orders a city-wide inquiry, questions the prophet Tiresias (who hints at the truth and is called a fraud for it), summons witnesses — and slowly unravels the case like a detective who never suspects the murderer is himself.

narrativeBlocks.title: The accumulating truth
narrativeBlocks.body: The pieces converge: Laius was killed at a crossroads where Oedipus once killed a rude stranger. A survivor's description of the attacker is one man, not bandits. A messenger brings news that his 'father' in Corinth died naturally — he was adopted. A shepherd confesses he once handed over a baby with pierced ankles.

narrativeBlocks.title: The answer: himself
narrativeBlocks.body: The investigation concludes that Oedipus is Laius's killer — and worse: Laius's son, exposed at birth to prevent a prophecy that he would kill his father and marry his mother. Every precaution Laius and Oedipus took produced exactly what it feared. Jocasta hangs herself; Oedipus blinds himself with her brooch-pins.

narrativeBlocks.title: Why the play endures
narrativeBlocks.body: Oedipus Rex is the first detective story — and its inversion: the detective is the criminal. Every generation re-reads the question of what self-knowledge costs.
